questions.s:
Consider the following statements on the late Harappan cultures :
I. The late Harappan cultures are primarily Chalcolithic in which tools of stone and copper are used.
II. They do not show metal objects requiring complicated casting.
III. The Chalcolithic people in the later Harappan phase lived in villages.
IV. In the late Harappan phase at Bhagwanpura in Haryana, burnt bricks were not found.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: Late Harappan cultures were rural Chalcolithic village cultures using stone and copper tools without complex metal casting. Statement IV is wrong because burnt bricks have been found at Bhagwanpura in Haryana.
questions.subject: History

questions.s:
Consider the following types of pottery :
I. Black and Red Ware
II. Black Slipped Ware
III. Painted Grey Ware
IV. Red Ware
V. Northern Black Polished Ware
Which of the above types of pottery were associated with the Later Vedic people ?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
questions.x: Later Vedic sites (c. 1000-600 BCE) yield Black and Red Ware, Black Slipped Ware, Painted Grey Ware (the hallmark) and Red Ware. Northern Black Polished Ware belongs to the later age of the Mahajanapadas and Mauryas.

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement on the contributions of Jainism :
o: The early Jainas adopted Prakrit to preach their doctrines.
Their religious literature was written in Ardhamagadhi.
The early Jainas discarded Sanskrit language.
They never used Apabhramsa for the earliest important works of Jainism.
questions.x: Jainas used Prakrit and Ardhamagadhi and avoided Sanskrit early on, but they did use Apabhramsa for many important works, so saying they never used it is incorrect.

Match the following :
List-I (Mahajanapada) - List-II (Capital)
A. Avanti - I. Ujjain
B. Koshala - II. Shravasti
C. Vatsa - III. Kaushambi
D. Anga - IV. Champa
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Avanti's capital was Ujjain, Koshala's Shravasti, Vatsa's Kaushambi and Anga's Champa.

questions.s:
Consider the following art and architectural forms :
I. Rock-cut elephant at Dhauli in Orissa
II. Yakshi figure from Didarganj near Patna
III. Great Stupa at Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh
IV. 80-pillared hall at Kumrahar near Patna
Which of the above art and architectural forms belong to the Mauryan period ?
questions.x: The Dhauli elephant, the polished Didarganj Yakshi, the original brick stupa at Sanchi (built under Ashoka) and the 80-pillared hall at Kumrahar (Pataliputra) are all Mauryan.

questions.s:
Consider the following items :
I. Turban
II. Trousers
III. Heavy long coat
IV. Helmet
V. Boots
Which of the items listed above were introduced by the Shakas and Kushans from Central Asia ?
o: I, II, III, IV and V
questions.x: The Central Asian Shakas and Kushans brought in cavalry-style dress: turban, tunic/trousers, heavy long coat, helmet and boots (R.S. Sharma).

questions.s: In the Satavahana's inscriptions, the terms 'Katakas' and 'Skandhavaras' mean
o: The tax free villages of Buddhist monks
Military camps and settlements which served as administrative centres
The areas of large scale paddy transplantations
questions.x: Satavahana inscriptions mention katakas and skandhavaras, which were military camps and settlements that also served as administrative centres.

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. During the reign of Chandragupta-I, the Sakas were defeated.
II. Samudragupta's South Indian conquest did not lead to any permanent annexation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The Sakas were defeated by Chandragupta-II, not Chandragupta-I. Samudragupta followed a policy of capture and release (grahana-moksha) in the south, so there was no permanent annexation.

questions.s: In the Sangam literature, Vellalars were :
o: rich peasants who formed the fourth caste
agricultural labourers who also worked with animal skins
forest tribes who suffered from extreme poverty
questions.x: Sangam texts describe the Vellalars as rich peasants (land-owning cultivators) who formed the fourth class of society.

Match the following :
List-I (Pallavan Ruler) - List-II (Political event)
A. Sivaskandavarman - I. Samudragupta's invasion
B. Vishnugopa - II. Kanchi came under the Pallavas
C. Narasimhavarman-I - III. Defeated by Vikramaditya-II and city of Kanchi was captured
D. Nandivarman-II - IV. Defeat of Pulakesin-II and destruction of Vatapi city
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Sivaskandavarman ruled from Kanchi, Vishnugopa of Kanchi faced Samudragupta, Narasimhavarman-I defeated Pulakesin-II and destroyed Vatapi, and Nandivarman-II lost Kanchi to the Chalukya Vikramaditya-II.

questions.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched with respect to Rashtrakutas ?
o: Amoghavarsha : the first Kannada book writer
Dantidurga : the founder of Rashtrakuta kingdom
Krishna-III : the famous rock-cut temple of Shiva at Ellora
questions.x: The rock-cut Kailasa (Shiva) temple at Ellora was built by Krishna-I, not Krishna-III. Amoghavarsha wrote Kavirajamarga, Dantidurga founded the dynasty and Al-Masudi wrote about the 'Balhara' (Vallabharaja) kings.

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement regarding the Cholas :
o: The Chola Empire was founded by Parantaka-I.
questions.x: The imperial Chola line was founded by Vijayalaya in the 9th century, not Parantaka-I. Parantaka-I took the title Maduraikonda after taking Madurai.

questions.s: Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi was built by :
questions.x: Qutb-ud-din Aibak built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque near the Qutb Minar in the 1190s; Iltutmish and Alauddin later extended it.

questions.x: Abdur Razzaq, envoy of the Timurid ruler Shah Rukh, visited Vijayanagara in 1442-43 during the reign of Devaraya-II.

A. Vallabhacharya - I. Uttar Pradesh
B. Tulsidas - II. Gujarat
C. Sri Chaitanya - III. Bengal
D. Tukaram - IV. Maharashtra
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :

Consider the following statements on Sher Shah's land revenue administration :
I. Land was classified into three categories on the basis of produce from the land.
II. Land was measured according to a uniform system.
III. 1/4 of the produce was collected as tax.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: Sher Shah measured land uniformly and classified it as good, middling and bad by produce. The state's share was one-third of the produce, not one-fourth.

questions.s:
Consider the following Mughal structures :
I. Tomb of Salim Chishti
II. Buland Darwaza
III. Tomb of Humayun
IV. Jami Masjid
Which of the above buildings were constructed during the reign of Akbar ?
questions.x: Salim Chishti's tomb, the Buland Darwaza and the Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri, and Humayun's tomb in Delhi (1565-72) were all built in Akbar's reign.

Match the following :
List-I (Name of the Ruler) - List-II (Position of the Ruler)
A. Husain Ali Khan - I. One of the Saiyid brothers
B. Murshid Quli Khan - II. The ruler of Bengal
C. Chin Qilich Khan - III. The Nizam of Hyderabad
D. Safdar Jung - IV. The Nawab of Awadh
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Husain Ali Khan was one of the Saiyid brothers, Murshid Quli Khan founded autonomous rule in Bengal, Chin Qilich Khan (Nizam-ul-Mulk) founded Hyderabad and Safdar Jung was Nawab of Awadh.

Match the following :
List-I (Kakatiya ruler) - List-II (Event / Contribution)
A. Rudradeva - I. Shifting the capital from Anamakonda to Orugallu (Warangal)
B. Ganapatideva - II. Thousand Pillar Temple was built
C. Rudramadevi - III. Malik Kafur's expedition
D. Prataparudradeva - IV. Marco Polo's visit to Coastal Andhra
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Rudradeva built the Thousand Pillar Temple at Hanamkonda, Ganapatideva moved the capital to Orugallu, Marco Polo visited Motupalli in Rudramadevi's time, and Malik Kafur attacked Warangal under Prataparudra.

questions.s: Identify the correct chronology of Later Mughals :
o: Bahadur Shah > Farrukh Siyar > Jahandar Shah > Muhammad Shah > Shah Alam-II
Bahadur Shah > Jahandar Shah > Muhammad Shah > Farrukh Siyar > Shah Alam-II
Bahadur Shah > Jahandar Shah > Farrukh Siyar > Muhammad Shah > Shah Alam-II
Farrukh Siyar > Jahandar Shah > Muhammad Shah > Shah Alam-II > Bahadur Shah
questions.x: Bahadur Shah I (1707-12) was followed by Jahandar Shah (1712-13), Farrukh Siyar (1713-19), Muhammad Shah (1719-48) and later Shah Alam II (1759-1806).

o: An officer responsible for intelligence, posts and household affairs
The in-charge of justice and charitable grants
The Master of Ceremonies and helped the king in foreign affairs

Consider the following Indian states :
I. Awadh
II. Jhansi
III. Satara
IV. Nagpur
V. Sindh
Which of the above states were annexed by the British due to the policy of Doctrine of Lapse ?
questions.x: Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur were annexed under Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse. Awadh was annexed on grounds of misgovernment and Sindh was conquered in 1843.

questions.s: Identify the wrong matching of poets and their languages in the 18th century :
questions.x: Dayaram was a Gujarati poet, not Marathi. Tayumanavar wrote in Tamil, Waris Shah (Heer Ranjha) in Punjabi and Kunchan Nambiar in Malayalam.

questions.s:
Consider the following statements on the contributions of Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar :
I. His great contribution was for the upliftment of women in India.
II. He organized a powerful movement for the enactment of Widow Remarriage Act.
III. To propagate his social ideas, he published Sambad Kaumudi, a Bengali weekly newspaper.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: Vidyasagar worked for women's education and led the campaign that produced the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856. Sambad Kaumudi was published by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, not Vidyasagar.
questions.subject: History

questions.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect on William Bentinck's reforms ?
o: Introduction of a new land revenue system in the North-Western Province
Establishment of universities for the first time
questions.x: Bentinck abolished sati (1829), acted against female infanticide and revised revenue settlement in the North-Western Provinces. The first universities came in 1857 under Canning.

questions.s:
Consider the following events :
I. Swadeshi Movement
II. Surat Split
III. Lucknow Pact
IV. Home Rule Movement
Which of the above main events took place during the extremist phase ?
questions.x: The extremist (militant nationalist) phase is dated 1905-1919/20, which covers the Swadeshi Movement (1905), Surat Split (1907), Lucknow Pact (1916) and Home Rule Movement (1916).

questions.s:
Consider the following events :
I. Visit of Simon Commission to India
II. Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore session
III. Launch of Dandi March
Which of the above main events took place during the tenure of Lord Irwin ?
questions.x: Lord Irwin was Viceroy from 1926 to 1931, covering the Simon Commission (1928), the Lahore Purna Swaraj resolution (1929) and the Dandi March (1930).

questions.s:
Consider the following Revolutionaries :
I. Bhagat Singh
II. Sachindra Nath Sanyal
III. Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee
IV. Ram Prasad Bismil
V. Chandra Shekhar Azad
Who among the above founded 'Hindustan Republican Association' in 1924 ?
questions.x: The Hindustan Republican Association was founded in 1924 at Kanpur by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Ram Prasad Bismil. Chandra Shekhar Azad joined it afterwards, and Bhagat Singh helped turn it into the HSRA in 1928. The final key is II, III and IV.
