questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid regarding the office of the 'Whip' ?
I. Although not mentioned in the Constitution of India, the office of the 'Whip' has however been incorporated in the Rules of the House by the 'Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognised Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act, 1998'.
II. The role of the Chief Whip of the government party in the Lok Sabha is served by the Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs.
III. All political parties - whether ruling or opposition, will have their own Whips in the Parliament.
IV. The Chief Whip is not responsible to the leader of the House but is responsible only to the leader of the party that has appointed him/her to the office of Chief Whip.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The whip is not mentioned in the Constitution or in the Rules of the House; it rests on parliamentary convention (the 1998 Act only gives facilities). Every party, ruling or opposition, has its own whip. The government's Chief Whip is the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs (not a Minister of State), and he works with the Leader of the House.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In the context of distinctions existing between a Public Bill and a Private Bill, select the statement/statements that is/are valid :
I. A Private Bill which has been introduced by a Member of Parliament sitting in the opposition and which has been approved by the House will have to be referred to the law department for consultation.
II. A Public Bill is always introduced in the Parliament by the Minister or a member of the government party.
III. A Private Bill will not reflect the policy of the government but upon its approval by the House, a Private Bill would have reflected the policy of the government.
IV. Public Bills and Private Bills, regardless of the differences between them, are governed by the same general procedure, and are required to be passed through the same stages in the House.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Public (government) bills are introduced only by ministers, and private members' bills by any non-minister MP; the drafting/law-department consultation applies to government bills. Both kinds go through the same general procedure and stages, so only IV is valid.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following State Bill/Bills will have to be mandatorily reserved for the President's consideration ?
I. A Bill that proposes to give effect to certain Directive Principles of State Policy.
II. A Bill requiring prior Presidential sanction but which was however not obtained under Article 304.
III. A Bill that attracts the provisions of Article 288.
IV. A Bill seeking to operate a provision that belongs to one of the Concurrent List entries, but which is however repugnant to any Union law.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Article 288(2) says a State law taxing water or electricity stored, generated or used by a Union authority has no effect unless it has been reserved for the President and received his assent, so such a bill must be reserved. In the other cases reservation is optional: the State only needs it if it wants the protection of Article 31A/31C or 254(2).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements in connection with the office of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) :
I. CAG can be removed by the President only in accordance with the procedure mentioned in the Constitution but this does not mean that the CAG can be impeached from office in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
II. Some public corporations are audited exclusively by private professional auditors, and the CAG may have no involvement at all.
III. The CAG can conduct legal, regulatory and propriety audit but not performance audit.
IV. The Constitution of India has not specified any criterion for the appointment of CAG.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
questions.x: Some corporations are audited only by private auditors with no CAG role, and the Constitution lays down no qualifications for the CAG. The CAG is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, and it does carry out performance audits, so I and III are wrong.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In connection with the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. The GST Council was established as a Statutory body, but it was later turned into a Constitutional federal body by an amendment of the Constitution.
II. The proceedings of the GST Council will be invalidated in the eventuality of any defect in the appointment of a person as a member of the Council.
III. In the event of any dispute between more than two states over GST issues, the GST Council has to refer the matter to be adjudicated by the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament.
IV. The GST Council is required to make recommendations to the Centre and the States on the threshold limit of turnover below which goods and services may be exempted from GST.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The GST Council was created directly by the 101st Amendment (Article 279A) and Article 279A(10) protects its proceedings from defects in appointments. Disputes go to a dispute settlement mechanism set up by the Council, not to the PAC. Recommending the turnover threshold for exemption is one of its listed functions.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Election Commission of India :
I. The Constitution of India has debarred the retiring Election Commissioners from any further appointment by the government.
II. In 'Anoop Baranwal Case' (2023), the Supreme Court has directed the Government to treat the Regional Commissioners on par with the Election Commissioners (other than the Chief Election Commissioner), as far as removal from office is concerned.
III. Since its inception, the Election Commission had functioned as a multi-member body.
IV. The power of superintendence, direction and control of elections to the office of Vice-President of India is vested in the Election Commission.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
questions.x: Under Article 324 the Election Commission controls elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. The Constitution does not bar retiring commissioners from later appointments, the Commission was single-member until 1989, and Anoop Baranwal dealt with the appointment process, not Regional Commissioners.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In the context of Centre - State Relations, which of the following statement/statements are valid ?
I. Punchhi Commission had recommended that the procedure that is followed for the removal of President should also be applicable for the impeachment of Governors as well.
II. The law that is made by the Parliament with respect to any matter in the State List in relation to the State in which President's rule is imposed, cannot be re-enacted by the State Legislature after the President's rule is ended.
III. The Sarkaria Commission was not the first to recommend the establishment of an Inter-State Council.
IV. Only the Lok Sabha can pass a resolution declaring that it is necessary in the national interest that the Parliament should make laws with respect to Goods and Services Tax.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Administrative Reforms Commission had recommended an Inter-State Council before the Sarkaria Commission did, so III is valid. A law made during President's rule can be altered by the State Legislature later, and a national-interest resolution under Article 249 is passed by the Rajya Sabha, so II and IV are wrong. The final key accepts only III; the preliminary key had also accepted I (the Punchhi Commission on impeaching Governors).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements in connection with the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States :
I. The proceeds of the surcharges that are levied on taxes and duties referred to in Article 269 and Article 270 of the Constitution of India, would be shared between the Centre and the States.
II. Article 268A and Article 272 of the Constitution of India were both repealed by same Constitutional Amendment Act.
III. Tax on the sale of petroleum crude is levied by the Centre but collected by the States.
IV. The net proceeds of tax categories that are falling under Article 269 of the Constitution of India, do not form a part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
questions.x: Taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States, so they do not enter the Consolidated Fund of India. Surcharges under Article 271 go wholly to the Centre, Article 272 was repealed by the 80th Amendment and 268A by the 101st, and petroleum crude is outside the State sales-tax scheme.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct in relation to the Human Rights Commissions in India ?
I. The role to undertake functions relating to human rights in the Union Territory of Ladakh may be conferred upon a State Human Rights Commission by the Central Government.
II. Only 2 persons can be appointed as members of the National Human Rights Commission under the category of possessing knowledge or practical experience with respect to human rights.
III. The President can remove the Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission on the ground of proved misbehaviour. However, the President has to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in this matter.
IV. The National Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into any matter after the expiry of two years from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: APPSC treated all four as incorrect. After the 2019 amendment the NHRC has three human-rights-expert members, not two. Commissions cannot inquire into a matter after one year, not two. The State Commission Chairperson is removed after a Supreme Court inquiry, not merely its opinion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements can be attributed correctly to the exercise of Delimitation ?
I. The principle of 'one man, one vote' reiterates the need for the exercise of Delimitation.
II. The Government of India can set up a Delimitation Commission for the purpose of delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies in a select few States or UTs.
III. The Delimitation Commission can only recommend the re-delimitation of territorial Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies but cannot recommend on the reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
IV. The Nodal Ministry for the Delimitation Commission of India is the Ministry of Law and Justice.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Delimitation gives effect to equal value of votes ('one man, one vote'), the Centre can constitute a commission for selected States/UTs (as in 2020 for J&K and the North-East), and the Ministry of Law and Justice is the nodal ministry. The Commission also decides which seats are reserved for SCs and STs, so III is wrong.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements with regard to India's Foreign Policy :
I. India's Act East Policy was originally conceived as an economic initiative but had later extended into political, strategic and cultural dimensions.
II. The 'Connect Central Asia Policy' has been taken forward with the institutionalization of the 'India-Central Asia Summit' mechanism.
III. Under the 'Security and Growth for All in the Region' (SAGAR) Policy, the DRDO initiated the Marine and Allied Interdisciplinary Training and Research Initiative (MAITRI) for the purpose of establishing long-term collaboration with countries in the East Asian region.
IV. India's Think West Policy is an outreach to the Western Industrialized nations for strengthening of relations in areas of education and defence.
Which of the above statements are valid ?
questions.x: Look East began as an economic policy and Act East added strategic and cultural dimensions, and the India-Central Asia Summit (2022) carries forward Connect Central Asia. MAITRI was started by INCOIS for Indian Ocean countries, not by DRDO for East Asia, and Think West concerns the Gulf/West Asia.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements can best describe the nature of security concerns/developments for India ?
I. The development of the Hambantota Development Zone can be seen or viewed as a policy of containment funded by Pakistan.
II. India's support in building the Chabahar port in Iran may serve as a strategic act to balance the Chinese-funded Gwadar port in Yemen.
III. Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) is an extension of the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) and serves as a platform for maritime security.
IV. The Malabar Exercise is connected with the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (QSD).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Since 2020 the Malabar naval exercise includes all four Quad members, linking it with the Quad. Hambantota was funded by China, Gwadar is in Pakistan (not Yemen), and IORA is an independent body, not part of ESCAP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In the context of Central Government programmes, which one of following statement/statements is/are incorrect ?
I. The objective of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) is aimed at reducing poverty of the ST communities by generating additional employment opportunities.
II. Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan Yojana (PM-SYM), monthly contribution is payable by the beneficiary, the State Government and the Central Government.
III. Under the 'FutureSkills Prime' Programme, Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) is the key implementing agency.
IV. Mission Karmayogi comprises of eight key pillars that are intended to create functional and behavioural competencies among the civil servants.
Select the answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: All four are incorrect. PM-AJAY is for Scheduled Castes, not STs. PM-SYM is funded 50:50 by the worker and the Centre only. FutureSkills Prime is run by MeitY with NASSCOM. Mission Karmayogi has six pillars.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In the context of the enactment of Budget, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. The Appropriation Bill carries an automatic repeal clause.
II. The provision 'Vote on Account' has become ineffectual after the re-scheduling of the budget cycle from the last day of February to the first day of February.
III. Amendments to either reject or reduce a tax can not be moved in case of the Finance Bill.
IV. The expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India can only be discussed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: An Appropriation Act lapses with the financial year, and charged expenditure can be discussed but not voted on. A vote on account is still used (for example in election years), and amendments to reduce or abolish a tax are allowed on the Finance Bill.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In connection with the veto power of the Indian President, which one of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. The Indian President possesses 'Suspensive Veto' in the case of Money Bills but not in the case of Finance Bills.
II. The Indian President can exercise 'Absolute Veto' with respect to the Government Bills at all times.
III. The Indian President enjoys 'Pocket Veto' indefinitely whereas the American President possesses 'Qualified Veto'.
IV. The objective of the veto power in being conferred upon the Indian President is to ensure a system of checks and balances between the office of the President and that of the power of the Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Constitution sets no time limit for presidential assent, so the Indian President has a pocket veto, while the US President has a qualified veto that Congress can override by a two-thirds majority. There is no suspensive veto for Money Bills, and an absolute veto is used only in special cases such as a bill whose government has fallen.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With reference to the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements :
I. It was intended to protect Central and State laws that are included in it from judicial review on the ground of violation of Fundamental rights.
II. The entries included in it are not restricted to the subject of land reforms and abolition of the zamindari system alone.
III. Article 31B carries a retrospective effect but it has ceased to be operative after the 'I.R. Coelho Case' (2007).
IV. The entries incorporated in it are only done so, by the power of the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.x: The Ninth Schedule (Article 31B, 1st Amendment) shields listed laws from challenge on fundamental-rights grounds, and it now includes many laws beyond land reform. Article 31B is still operative (Coelho only allows basic-structure review of laws added after 24 April 1973), and entries are added by Parliament through constitutional amendment, not by the Central Government.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
The 'Territory of India' and the 'Union of India' are two distinct and different expressions due to which of the following reason/reasons ?
I. The 'Union of India' includes just States and Union Territories while the 'Territory of India' includes in addition to States and Union Territories, those territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any future time as well.
II. The expression 'Union of India' is mentioned in the Constitution of India, but the expression 'Territory of India' is not found in the Constitution of India.
III. The First Schedule of the Constitution of India is with reference to just the 'Union of India' but not the 'Territory of India'.
IV. The Union Territories are covered by the expression 'Territory of India' and not by the expression 'Union of India'.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under Article 1 the 'Union of India' means only the States, while the 'Territory of India' covers the States, the Union Territories and any acquired territory. So Union Territories fall under the Territory of India but not the Union, and both expressions appear in the Constitution and in the First Schedule.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With reference to Indian polity, which one of the following statements would you accept as appropriate ideas referring to 'Equality' ?
I. The primacy of equality is safeguarded, defined and enforced by the courts of law rather than by the Constitution as conceptualized by A.V. Dicey.
II. Article 14 of the Constitution of India constitutes only the concept of 'Equality before the law' but does not mention the concept of 'Equal Protection of Laws'.
III. Article 194 and Article 361A of the Constitution of India are indicative of the fact that equality in India is not absolute.
IV. The theory of equality includes distinction of merit but not distinction on account of hereditary titles or nobility as propounded by the Balaji Raghavan Case (1995).
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Legislative privileges (Article 194) and the press immunity for reporting legislative proceedings (Article 361A) are exceptions to equality, and Balaji Raghavan (1995) upheld national awards as recognition of merit while barring hereditary titles. Article 14 contains both 'equality before law' and 'equal protection of laws', and in India equality is guaranteed by the Constitution itself.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are correct with regard to the Fundamental Duties ?
I. Fundamental Duties are confined to just the citizens of India with the exception of Article 51A(i), which is also applicable to foreigners that are resident in India.
II. The Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties of the Citizens (1999) had recommended the implementation of the Fundamental Duties irrespective of the existence of legal provisions.
III. In 'Kesavananda Bharati' Case (1973), the Supreme Court of India held that the Fundamental Duties may be used to decide the constitutionality of laws that are otherwise ambiguous to interpret.
IV. The Sardar Swaran Singh Committee had recommended for penalties to be considered in the eventuality of non-compliance of any of the Fundamental Duties.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended that Parliament provide penalties for non-compliance with the duties. All fundamental duties apply only to citizens, the Verma Committee identified existing legal provisions for enforcing them, and Fundamental Duties were added only in 1976, after Kesavananda.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With regards to Directive Principles of State Policy, what is the correct chronological order in which the following additions/changes were incorporated into the Constitution of India through amendments ?
I. The adding of a second aspect relating to Article 38.
II. The changing of the subject-matter of Article 45.
III. The adding of Article 43B.
IV. The adding of Article 48A.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Article 48A came with the 42nd Amendment (1976), Article 38(2) with the 44th (1978), the new Article 45 on early childhood care with the 86th (2002), and Article 43B on co-operative societies with the 97th (2011).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The 25th Constitutional Amendment Act (1971) inserted a new Article 31C, whose first provision was declared as invalid by the Supreme Court in the Keshavananda Bharati Case (1973).
II. The Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills Case (1980) considered the extension of the scope of the second provision of Article 31C as invalid as well.
III. The Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills Case (1980) has considered the importance of harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
IV. The present interpretation with respect to the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is the same reiteration of the principle that was first propounded by the Supreme Court in the Chamapakan Dorairajan case (1951).
Which of the statement/statements given above is/are incorrect ?
questions.x: Minerva Mills (1980) did stress harmony and balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, so statement III is correct. Kesavananda struck down the second provision of Article 31C (the bar on judicial review), not the first. Minerva Mills struck down the 42nd Amendment's widening of the first provision, not the second. Champakam Dorairajan had made the Directive Principles subordinate to Fundamental Rights, so the present view is not a restatement of it. That makes I, II and IV the incorrect ones.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
With reference to the procedure for Amendment of the Constitution, consider the following statements :
I. A private member of the House of the Parliament can introduce the Bill for amendment of the Constitution only after the prior permission of the President.
II. Article 368 of the Constitution of India provides for three types of amendments - simple majority, special majority and ratification of half of the States by a simple majority.
III. For amendments that require ratification of half the States by a simple majority, it is not necessary that all the State Legislatures must take action on the Bill.
IV. The State Legislatures can pass a resolution requesting the Parliament to amend Article 368 in the same manner, as it could be done for the creation or abolition of Legislative Councils in the States.
Which of the statement/statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.x: Once half of the States ratify, the amendment can proceed even if other States do not act. A private member needs no prior presidential permission, Article 368 itself covers only special majority and special majority plus ratification, and States cannot initiate amendments.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following statements about the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution :
I. The doctrine of the 'Basic Structure' has been incorporated into the Constitution of India by an Act of Parliament.
II. Presently, the Parliament under Article 368 of the Constitution of India can amend any part of the Constitution without affecting the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.
III. Parliament's limited power to amend the Constitution is also an element of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.
IV. The Supreme Court in the 'Kumar Padma Prasad Case' (1992) has declared that the mandate to build a 'welfare state' is an element of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct ?
questions.x: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution as long as the basic structure is not destroyed, and Minerva Mills held that this limited amending power is itself part of the basic structure. The doctrine is judge-made, not enacted, and Kumar Padma Prasad was about the independence of the judiciary, not the welfare state.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s: Which of the following statement is correct regarding Parliamentary Privileges ?
o: Parliamentary Privileges are the privileges that are enjoyed collectively by each House of the Parliament, and not by the Members individually.
Only Members can be punished for contempt by reprimand and admonition but not outsiders.
The phrase 'Breach of Privilege' has wider implications than the 'Contempt of the House'.
The Members cannot be arrested during the session of Parliament but this privilege is available only in civil cases and not in criminal cases or preventive detention cases.
questions.x: Freedom from arrest (during a session and 40 days before and after) covers only civil cases, not criminal or preventive detention cases. Privileges are both collective and individual, outsiders can be punished for contempt, and contempt is the wider idea.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
The equal status of the Rajya Sabha with the Lok Sabha can be described by which of the following statement/statements ?
I. Introduction and passage of Money Bills.
II. Consideration of the CAG's report.
III. Initiating the removal of the Vice-President.
IV. Approval of proclamation of all the three types of emergencies by the President.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Both Houses have equal powers to consider CAG reports and to approve proclamations of national, State and financial emergency. Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and the resolution to remove the Vice-President can start only in the Rajya Sabha (a special power, not equality).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following source/sources of revenue qualifies/qualify for being given to the Panchayats ?
I. The tax proceeds that are assigned to the States from the Centre may be again re-distributed to the Panchayats as recommended by the Central Finance Commission.
II. Loans from the State Government.
III. Under Article 243-I of the Constitution of India, the State Government is empowered to devolve its own funds to the Panchayats even in the absence of the State Finance Commission's recommendations.
IV. Internal Resource Generation is facilitated only in the case of Panchayats situated in Scheduled Areas as per the Fifth Schedule.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Panchayats can receive loans from the State Government. Sharing of State taxes with Panchayats is decided on the State Finance Commission's advice under Article 243-I, and all Panchayats, not only those in Scheduled Areas, can raise their own revenue.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : In connection with their own resource collection, the Panchayats at the village level are better placed than the Panchayats at the Intermediate and the District levels.
Reason (R) : The Gram Panchayats have their own tax domain whereas the other two tiers have to depend only on tolls, fees and non-tax revenue for internal resource generation.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: In most States only Gram Panchayats are given real taxing powers (house tax, property tax and so on), while the intermediate and district tiers depend on fees, tolls and grants. That is why village Panchayats are better placed to raise their own resources.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In connection with the lapsing of Bills, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. If the Lok Sabha has passed the Bill, but if the Bill has still not been discussed in the Rajya Sabha, then such a Bill does not lapse.
II. A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration of the Houses will not lapse. However, the Lok Sabha should not have been dissolved by the time the Bill is returned.
III. A Bill that is passed by both the Houses but pending for President's assent will not lapse.
IV. A Bill that is pending in the Rajya Sabha but which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha will also lapse.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The preliminary key gave option 1 (Only III). On dissolution of the Lok Sabha a bill passed by both Houses and awaiting assent does not lapse. A bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha lapses, a bill returned by the President does not lapse even if the Lok Sabha has been dissolved, and a Rajya Sabha bill not yet passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are incorrect regarding the Law Commission of India ?
I. It is a non-constitutional quasi judicial body.
II. One of its functions is to communicate its opinion to the President on subjects relating to legal administration.
III. Its reports are not submitted to the Parliament.
IV. It has no suo motu decision power to undertake research by itself.
Select the answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Law Commission is a non-statutory advisory (not quasi-judicial) body set up by executive order. It reports to the Government through the Ministry of Law and Justice, its reports are laid before Parliament, and it can take up studies suo motu, so all four statements are incorrect.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid with respect to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution ?
I. The term 'democratic' as used in the Preamble is a mix of British Fabian Socialism and American Populism.
II. The term 'Republic' in the Preamble indicates that India has an elected head, called the Prime Minister.
III. The 'Liberty' expressed in the Preamble is neither absolute nor qualified.
IV. The term 'Fraternity' as used by the Preamble, originally denoted the dignity of the individual only.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: None is valid. 'Democratic' in the Preamble covers political, social and economic democracy, not Fabian socialism. 'Republic' means an elected head of state, the President. Liberty in the Preamble is qualified, not absolute. Fraternity originally meant both the dignity of the individual and the unity of the nation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.s:
In recent times, many leading agencies have reaffirmed high growth for the Indian Economy. Which of the following statement/statements can be the best reason/reasons for India's projected high growth ?
I. Strong Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE)
II. Government's shift of focus from large capital expenditure towards private investment
III. Increase in domestic air passenger traffic along with a reduction in the volume of Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG)
IV. Fading of the El Nino oscillation and better Rabi crop prospects
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Agencies pointed to strong private consumption and the fading El Nino with better rabi prospects. The government kept up high public capital expenditure rather than shifting away from it, and FMCG volumes were rising, not falling.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
With regard to the progress of Digital Payments in India, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. Promotion of Digital Payments has been transferred from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to the Department of Financial Services.
II. e-RUPI is an institution-based voucher management system instead of being person and purpose specific.
III. 'Hello! UPI' is an AI voice-enabled payment feature built by a consortium of private sponsored startups recognised by the NPCI.
IV. 'UPI LITE X' addresses challenges of remote areas by enabling offline UPI payments.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: In 2023 the work of promoting digital payments moved from MeitY to the Department of Financial Services, and UPI Lite X lets people pay offline in remote areas. e-RUPI is person- and purpose-specific, and 'Hello! UPI' was launched by NPCI itself.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Tourism in India has turned out to be a key service sub-sector. Which of the following statements are valid regarding the Tourism sector in India ?
I. NIDHI is a technology-driven system meant for providing services to Hospitality and Travel industry.
II. The Government has resolved to make India a one trillion USD tourism economy by 2047 with 100 million international investors.
III. The Hotel Occupancy Rate has been rapidly increasing alongside a consistent rise in the average daily rate and revenue per available room.
IV. India's Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) has been in the expanding zone.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: NIDHI (National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry) is a technology platform for the hospitality sector, and the services PMI has stayed in the expansion zone, above 50. The final key does not accept II (the USD 1 trillion tourism economy by 2047 goes with 100 million international tourists, not investors) or III. The final key is I and IV.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
The Interim Union Budget (FY25) has proposed initiatives to boost India's Green Energy Sector. Which of the following proposals are connected with developing India's Green Energy ?
I. Viability Gap Funding (VGF) for utilizing solar energy projects
II. To set up coal gasification and liquefaction capacity of 100MT by 2030
III. Optional blending of Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) in Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) for transport and Piped Natural Gas (PNG) for domestic purposes
IV. Provision of financial assistance for procurement of biomass aggregation machinery
V. Setting up of a payment security system for expanding the bio-manufacturing system in the country
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Interim Budget 2024 proposed 100 MT coal gasification and liquefaction capacity by 2030 and financial help to buy biomass aggregation machinery. The VGF was for offshore wind, CBG blending was to be mandatory and phased, and the bio-manufacturing plan was a new scheme, not a payment security system.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statement can best be described as having resulted in the recovery of India's external sector ?
o: Moderation in India's merchandise export growth in FY24 accompanied by a sharp decline in India's merchandise import growth
Increasing commodity prices with escalating global demand
Increase in merchandise exports and imports followed by a decline in net services receipts
Growth in world output outpacing the world trade volume
questions.x: In FY24 merchandise imports fell faster than exports slowed, which narrowed the trade and current account deficits. That is what the Economic Review credited for the external sector's recovery.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : Tax reforms directed towards a simple tax system will result in positive productivity gains.
Reason (R) : They boost GDP growth and employment growth by removing deadweight costs and reduce distortions in resource allocation.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains A.
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: A simpler tax system cuts deadweight losses and distortions in how resources are allocated. That raises productivity, GDP growth and employment, so R explains A.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid regarding the National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) ?
I. NIP includes only economic infrastructure projects but not social infrastructure projects.
II. NIP is aimed to focus on key greenfield projects alone. Brownfield projects are excluded from the NIP's coverage.
III. NIP aims to offer investment opportunities in India's infrastructure sector, and to attract investments into India.
IV. India Investment Grid (IIG) as a platform has ceased to facilitate the NIP and instead 'Invest India' is presently facilitating NIP.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The NIP covers both economic and social infrastructure and both greenfield and brownfield projects, and NIP projects are shown to investors on the India Investment Grid. Its aim is to offer infrastructure investment opportunities and attract investment, so only III is valid.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : Majority of the reported transactions on e-NAM are intra-mandi instead of inter-mandi and inter-state.
Reason (R) : The Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (APLM) Act, 2017 provides for progressive agricultural marketing reforms that include greater focus on intra-mandi transactions.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: Most e-NAM trades are still within one mandi. The model APLM Act, 2017 aims at a single unified market with inter-mandi and inter-state trade, not a focus on intra-mandi deals, so R is false.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: The strategic objective of Asset Monetization Programme may be explained as :
o: An initiative to unlock the value of investments in private sector assets by utilizing public sector capital.
Involving an indefinite period license/lease of an asset, owned by the government or a public authority, to a private sector entity.
Facilitating an opportunity for public asset owners to use new financial structures by utilizing capital from private sector investors.
Offering an alternative mechanism to the PPP model.
questions.x: The National Monetisation Pipeline aims to unlock the value of brownfield public assets by bringing in private capital through structures such as InvITs and OMDA contracts. It uses limited-period licences, and ownership stays with the government.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
In connection with SEBI, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. SEBI exempted regulations for Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) and Muncipal Bonds in order to facilitate more efficient infrastructure financing through the capital markets.
II. SEBI introduced the framework in which listed large corporates will mandatorily meet 25% of their financing requirements through the issuance of debt securities.
III. SEBI increased the minimum ticket size of corporate bond investment in order to encourage investor responsibility.
IV. SEBI along with the RBI introduced the Retail Direct Scheme.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under SEBI's large corporate framework, listed large corporates must raise at least 25% of their incremental borrowings through debt securities. SEBI eased (not exempted) the InvIT and municipal bond rules and cut the minimum ticket size of corporate bonds, and the Retail Direct Scheme is an RBI scheme.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : 'India Stack' has enabled an online, paperless and cashless digital access to various public and private services. This has reduced the cost of conducting e-KYC.
Reason (R) : India Stack consists of two interconnected layers, and of these, the 'Payment Layer' has reduced the cost of conducting e-KYC.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: India Stack has made paperless, cashless access to services possible and cut e-KYC costs. But it has three layers (identity, payments and data), and the cheaper e-KYC comes from the identity layer (Aadhaar), not the payment layer.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s: Pick the correct sequence out of the following sequences with regard to the present prevailing inflation trends (in percentages) in India :
o: Food Inflation > Headline Inflation > Core Inflation
Headline Inflation > Food Inflation > Core Inflation
Core Inflation > Food Inflation > Headline Inflation
questions.x: In early 2024 food inflation was around 8-9%, headline CPI around 5% and core inflation below 4%, so food > headline > core.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid in connection with inflation ?
I. Cost-push inflation cycle of milk is becoming more and more pronounced in India.
II. The Bharat Atta initiative of the Government has played a considerable role in containing wheat inflation in India.
III. Retail Inflation has considerably increased in the beginning of 2024 owing to increasing commodity prices.
IV. The Bharat Dal initiative has also been extended to include moong dal.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Subsidised Bharat Atta sales helped contain wheat prices and the Bharat Dal scheme was extended to moong dal. The final key also accepts III (retail inflation rising at the beginning of 2024 on commodity prices), which the preliminary key had not; I is not accepted. The final key is II, III and IV.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid in connection with Enhanced Access and Service Excellence (EASE) Reforms ?
I. EASE Reforms are governed by a board of directors, who are heads of premier Financial Institutions in India.
II. EASE Next programme had just one (01) priority - the Common Reforms Agenda.
III. Delivering excellence in customer service with digital enablement is one of the four themes conceptualized as part of EASE 6.0.
IV. EASE Reforms are intended for both Public Sector Banks (PSBs) as well as NBFCs.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: EASE 6.0 has four themes, one of which is customer service excellence with digital enablement. EASE is a reform agenda for public sector banks only, steered by the Department of Financial Services and IBA, and EASE Next had more than one priority.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following feature/features is/are correct regarding Stand-Up India Scheme ?
I. This scheme covers brownfield enterprises along with greenfield enterprises.
II. Non-Individual enterprises are also eligible to avail the benefit of this scheme provided certain conditions are complied with.
III. For drawal of Working Capital up to ₹ 10 lakh, the same may be sanctioned by way of Cash Credit Limit.
IV. Besides Primary Security, the loan may be secured by a guarantee of Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India Loans (CGFSIL) as decided by the banks.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Non-individual enterprises qualify if at least 51% is held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur, and loans can be backed by CGFSIL cover. The scheme is only for greenfield enterprises, and working capital up to ₹10 lakh is given through an overdraft, not cash credit.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RBI's Digital Payments Index (RBI-DPI) :
I. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has been publishing the RBI-DPI with 2021 as the base year to capture the extent of digitisation of payments across the country.
II. The RBI-DPI consists of 6 broad parameters that have in turn sub-parameters.
III. There has been a constant increase in the RBI-DPI since the time of its inception.
IV. 'Consumer Centricity' is one of the parameters in the RBI-DPI.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
questions.x: The RBI-DPI has risen steadily since it began, and Consumer Centricity is one of its parameters. Its base period is March 2018, not 2021, and it has five broad parameters, not six.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements qualifies/qualify as valid in connection with the banking mechanism in India ?
I. Increasing the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) will result in increasing credit creation.
II. Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) applies only to the new deposit base while the Incremental Cash Reserve Ratio (ICRR) specifically targets the new borrower lending base.
III. 'Tenor Premium' is an important component in the calculation of the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR).
IV. Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) is used as a long-term policy rate and is generally lower than the Bank Rate.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: MCLR is built from the marginal cost of funds, the negative carry on CRR, operating costs and a tenor premium. A higher CRR reduces credit creation, CRR applies to all net demand and time liabilities, and MSF is an overnight window at the same rate as the Bank Rate.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
In the context of India's fight against poverty, consider the following statements :
I. Unlike the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI), the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) developed by NITI Aayog does not make use of 'Alkire-Foster' (AF) methodology.
II. The urban population witnessed a larger decline in poverty as compared to the rural population.
III. Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package (PMGKP) includes the coverage of food grain entitlements.
IV. The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is computed by adding the incidence of multidimensional poverty and the intensity of poverty.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid ?
questions.x: PMGKP included free food grains under PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana. NITI Aayog's MPI also uses the Alkire-Foster method, rural poverty fell faster than urban poverty, and MPI is the product (not the sum) of incidence and intensity.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
In connection with the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF), which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. The fund will be established through reserved bonds taken from the G-Sec market.
II. The fund is to be exclusively availed by private agencies to create urban infrastructure in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
III. Eligible activities for UIDF shall be connected to the Missions and Programmes of the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA).
IV. The fund will be collectively managed by a cluster of Municipal Cooperative Banks.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: UIDF is funded from shortfalls in priority sector lending and managed by the National Housing Bank. Public agencies use it for urban infrastructure in Tier 2 and 3 cities, and eligible activities are linked to MoHUA missions.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
With regard to the Startup Ecosystem in India, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE) Centre will not be presiding over the selection process of the applications that are received under Startup Agri-Business Incubation Programme.
II. Mentorship, Advisory, Assistance, Resilience and Growth (MAARG) Portal is an exclusive one-stop platform intended for guiding startups in the emerging Aritificial Intelligence (AI) sector only.
III. Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) aims to provide financial assistance to startups for conducting 'proof of concept' trials.
IV. Fund of Funds Scheme (FFS) for Startups is meant to contribute to various Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) registered with the SEBI.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme funds proof of concept, prototypes and product trials, and the Fund of Funds for Startups invests through SEBI-registered AIFs. MANAGE does run selection for its agri-business incubation programme, and MAARG is a mentorship portal for startups in all sectors.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : The National Product measures all goods and services that arise out of economic activity, whereas National Income is the sum of all incomes as a result of the economic activity. These two are synonymous.
Reason (R) : The Production of goods and services is the outcome of the use of capital and labour, along with the raw materials, and this automatically generates income.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: The value of goods and services produced is paid out as wages, rent, interest and profit to the factors used, so national product equals national income. Because production automatically creates income, R explains A.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid regarding the prevailing scenarios and issues in connection with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ?
I. The 'Peace Clause' under the Bali Agreement reiterates that developing nations must not exceed the 10% ceiling limit for Public Stockholding schemes initiatives.
II. The 'Green Box' prohibits the use of direct payments to producers which are not linked to production decisions.
III. The 'Reduction Commitments' are expressed in terms of a "Total Aggregate Measurement of Support" which includes all product-specific support and non-product-specific support in one single figure.
IV. Any support that would normally be placed in the 'Amber Box', is not to be placed in the 'Blue Box' even if the support mandates farmers to limit production.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Under the Agreement on Agriculture, reduction commitments are stated as a Total AMS that combines product-specific and non-product-specific support. The Bali peace clause protects developing countries from challenge even if public stockholding breaches the 10% limit, the Green Box allows decoupled direct payments, and Amber Box support that limits production moves to the Blue Box.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the correct code :
Assertion (A) : Coal washing results in increased generation efficiency and reduced investment costs. However, the use of washed coal in India is still limited.
Reason (R) : The limited establishment of coal washeries may be attributed to the perception that coal washing by increasing the cost of electricity generation, would adversely impact the plants in terms of 'merit order' scheduling.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not explain (A).
questions.x: Washed coal burns more efficiently and lowers capital and maintenance costs, yet little is used. Generators fear that the extra washing cost raises their per-unit tariff and pushes them down the merit-order dispatch list, which explains the slow uptake.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid in connection with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) ?
I. Achieving Goal 10 will require an entire reform of the financial system that promotes equitable pay and decent work for young people.
II. NITI Aayog has developed the National Indicator Framework (NIF) for facilitating monitoring of SDGs in India.
III. 'Mission LiFE' aims to influence government and industrial policy to support both sustainable consumption and production.
IV. The concept of global citizenship embedded in Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4) is a reference term that indicates flexible citizenship rights across countries for the purpose of facilitating better labour markets.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Mission LiFE seeks to change individual behaviour and to shape government and industrial policy towards sustainable consumption and production. The National Indicator Framework was developed by MoSPI, not NITI Aayog, decent work for youth is SDG 8 (not 10), and 'global citizenship' in SDG 4 is about education values, not rights to move between countries.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are valid regarding Human Development ?
I. Two countries with the same level of Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, but ending with different human development outcomes is indicative of the importance of growth over development.
II. A country's score on the Inequality-Adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) is not the same as its Human Development Index (HDI) even when there is no inequality among people.
III. In Gender Development Index (GDI), values below 1 indicate higher development for women than men.
IV. Planetary Pressures-adjusted Human Development Index (PHDI) focuses on intergenerational inequality just the same way, as the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI) focuses on intragenerational inequality.
V. According to the Human Development Report 2021 - 22, a new uncertainty complex is emerging, which comprises of three new concerns — planetary changes, sweeping social transformations and polarized societies.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: UNDP describes the PHDI as a measure of intergenerational inequality, just as the IHDI measures inequality within a generation, and HDR 2021-22 names a new uncertainty complex of planetary change, social transformation and polarisation. Same income with different outcomes shows policy choices matter beyond growth, IHDI equals HDI when there is no inequality, and a GDI below 1 means women are behind men.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are valid regarding the interventions of the Government of Andhra Pradesh in the context of Healthcare ?
I. Telemedicine facility is available in all Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs) to avail specialist services through district hub.
II. The Family Doctor Programme has been planned to be implemented as a standalone project without the need to be integrated with Primary Health Centres (PHCs).
III. Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Scheme has been revamped, by increasing the income limit from ₹ 2.5 lakh to ₹ 5 lakh per annum per family.
IV. 'Aarogya Aasara' Scheme is intended to provide post-operative sustenance allowance with certain eligible conditions complied with.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: AP offers telemedicine through its health and wellness centres linked to district hubs, raised the Aarogyasri income ceiling to ₹5 lakh, and pays a post-operative sustenance allowance under Aarogya Aasara. The Family Doctor Programme works through the PHCs, not as a standalone project.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
In connection with transport and infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh, which of the following statement/statements is/are valid ?
I. Andhra Pradesh's first riverine project has been proposed between Muktyala and Madipadu on Krishna river.
II. The Bhogapuram Greenfield International Airport had been started with a corpus fund that is sourced from National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF).
III. Infrastructure investments in Andhra Pradesh are strictly implemented only with reference to strategic investments like ports and industrial corridors, but not with reference to community assets.
IV. Rail Over Bridges (ROBs) are being developed in Andhra Pradesh under the Setu Bandhan Scheme.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Muktyala-Madipadu stretch of the Krishna was proposed as the State's first riverine (inland waterway) project, and ROBs are being built under the Setu Bandhan scheme. Bhogapuram airport is a PPP project by GMR, not funded from an NIIF corpus, and AP also invests in community assets.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are incorrect regarding the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Policy 2023 - 27 ?
I. To achieve a minimum contribution of 25% by industry in the State GDP
II. To provide end-to-end facilitation in 2 weeks
III. To envisage ten (10) priorities of accomplishment
IV. To focus on becoming a 'Plug and Play State' for investments
V. Ensuring land allotment by APIIC within a period of 2 weeks upon receipt of application
Select the answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The AP Industrial Development Policy 2023-27 does aim to make AP a 'plug and play' state for investors. The share target, facilitation timeline, number of priorities and APIIC land-allotment period given in I, II, III and V do not match the policy, so APPSC keyed them as incorrect.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statements are valid in connection with Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy (2023) ?
I. The objective is to target Green Energy production up to the capacity of 1 MPTA (Million Tonnes Per Annum) or Green Ammonia production up to the capacity of 2.0 MPTA in the next five years.
II. New and Renewable Energy Development Corporation of A.P. Ltd (NREDCAP) shall act as a Nodal Agency under this policy.
III. All the Ports in the State have infrastructure for storing liquid nitrogen which can then be utilized for storing Green Hydrogen for exporting to other countries.
IV. The Policy prohibits the production of Green Hydrogen/Green Ammonia by using Renewable Energy and/or Biomass from 'Third-Party/Power exchange'.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: NREDCAP is the nodal agency under the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy 2023, and the official key also accepted III about port storage infrastructure. The policy targets 0.5 MTPA green hydrogen or 2 MTPA green ammonia, and it allows renewable power from third parties or power exchanges.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are valid regarding the socio-economic status of Andhra Pradesh ?
I. Andhra Pradesh won the Best State Award of ICAR - National Research Center for Banana (NRCB) for export promotion.
II. Andhra Pradesh GSDP growth rate has been registering a decline in recent times owing to repeated lower returns in certain sub-sectors of the Service Sector.
III. For the FY 2024 - 25, the Revenue Deficit is budgeted higher than the Fiscal Deficit in terms of percentage of Andhra Pradesh GSDP.
IV. The technology used by the Government of Andhra Pradesh while conducting resurvey of landholdings is referred to as 'Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS)' technology.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: AP received ICAR-NRCB's best state award for banana export promotion, and its land resurvey uses the CORS network. AP's GSDP growth has been high, not falling, and the revenue deficit is always smaller than the fiscal deficit.
questions.subject: Economy

questions.s:
Following are the intrusive landforms of volcanic activity and their characteristic features :
I. Batholiths : Huge mass of igneous rocks, usually granite at the deeper layers of the crust.
II. Phacoliths : Large igneous mounds with a dome-shaped upper surface.
III. Dykes : Wall-like structures developed by solidifying almost perpendicular to the ground.
IV. Sills : The near horizontal bodies of intrusive igneous rocks.
Which of the above are correctly matched ?
questions.x: Batholiths, dykes and sills are described correctly (NCERT). Large dome-topped igneous mounds are laccoliths; phacoliths are wavy lens-shaped masses at the crests and troughs of folds.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Silicon and oxygen are common elements in all types of feldspar and sodium, potassium, calcium, aluminium etc. are found in specific feldspar variety.
II. Almost one-fourth of the Earth's crust is composed of feldspar and quartz.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: All feldspars contain silicon and oxygen, with sodium, potassium, calcium or aluminium depending on the type. Feldspar alone makes up about half of the crust (NCERT) and quartz about 12%, so 'one-fourth' is wrong.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement :
o: Geomorphic processes bring about changes in the configuration of the surface of the Earth.
Diastrophism and volcanism are endogenic geomorphic processes.
The endogenic and exogenic forces cause physical stresses and chemical actions on earth materials.
Orogeny is the continental building process.
questions.x: Orogeny is mountain building through severe folding. Continent building is epeirogeny, so statement 4 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Soil formation is controlled by the following factors :
I. Parent material
II. Topography
III. Climate
IV. Biological activity
V. Time
Which of the above are active factors ?
questions.x: Climate and biological activity are the active factors of soil formation. Parent material, topography and time are passive (controlling) factors.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List-I (Clouds) - List-II (Description)
A. Cirrus - I. Milky appearance
B. Cirrostratus - II. Silky appearance
C. Cirrocumulus - III. Cauliflower structure
D. Cumulus - IV. Small globular masses
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Cirrus clouds are thin and silky, cirrostratus form a milky sheet, cirrocumulus appear as small white globules, and cumulus have a cauliflower-like structure.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Doldrums are the strong winds that have rapid surface movement.
II. The prevailing trade wind direction in northern hemisphere is northwest.
Which of the above statements is/are correct ?
questions.x: The doldrums are the calm equatorial low-pressure belt with weak winds, and the northern trade winds blow from the northeast. So both statements are wrong.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement on extra-tropical cyclones :
o: These develop in the mid and high latitudes.
They do not have a clear frontal system.
They affect a large area as compared to the tropical cyclones.
They can originate over the land and sea.
questions.x: Extra-tropical (temperate) cyclones form along fronts where warm and cold air masses meet, so they have a clear frontal system. It is tropical cyclones that lack fronts.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following :
I. Dry winter season
II. No dry season
III. Dry hot summer
IV. Dry and very severe winter
Which of the above are not the characteristic features of Mediterranean Climate ?
questions.x: Mediterranean climate (Cs) has hot dry summers and mild rainy winters. So a dry winter, no dry season and a severe dry winter are not its features.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Guyot is :
o: A mountain with pointed summit rising from the seafloor that does not reach the surface of the ocean.
A deep valley sometimes found cutting across the continental shelves and slopes.
A flat topped seamount showing the evidence of gradual subsidence through stages.
A low island found in the tropical oceans consisting of coral reefs surrounding a central depression.
questions.x: A guyot is a flat-topped seamount whose top was eroded at sea level and then sank gradually. The other options describe a seamount, a submarine canyon and an atoll.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. In general, the terrigenous deposits are derived from the land and are mainly deposited on the continental shelves.
II. From the shore onwards, there is a gradual increase in the coarseness of the terrigenous deposits.
III. The muds, the finest materials, are the terrigenous deposits.
IV. The colouring of the muds depends upon their chemical content.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: Terrigenous deposits come from the land and settle mainly on the continental shelves, muds are the finest of them, and mud colour depends on chemical content. They get finer, not coarser, away from the shore.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. The Great Rift Valley in East Africa forms a series of lakes.
II. Most of these lakes are fresh water lakes.
III. Lake Malawi is at the southern end in the Rift Valley.
IV. Lake Victoria, the largest one, is a part of the Rift Valley.
Which of the above statements are correct ?
questions.x: The preliminary key gave option 1 (I, II and III). The East African Rift holds a chain of lakes, most of them freshwater, with Lake Malawi at its southern end. Lake Victoria lies in a shallow basin between the two rift arms, not in the rift itself.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following countries :
I. Chile
II. Venezuela
III. Ecuador
IV. Peru
V. Colombia
Which of the above South American countries have a Pacific coastline ?
questions.x: Chile, Ecuador, Peru and Colombia border the Pacific. Venezuela's coast is on the Caribbean Sea.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement :
o: Taiga is the largest land biome in the world.
This cold biome stretches across the northern portion of North America, Europe and Asia.
Within this biome, there is a narrow range of temperatures between the winter and summer seasons.
Precipitation in this biome is moderately high throughout the year with snow occurring during the winter months.
questions.x: The taiga has a very large annual temperature range, with very cold winters and short mild summers. So a 'narrow range' is incorrect. The final key accepts both option 3 and option 4.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Himalayas are correct ?
I. Himalayas are geologically young and structurally fold mountains.
II. They are wide in Kashmir and narrow in the North-eastern states.
III. The folds of Great Himalayas are asymmetrical in nature and their core is composed of granite.
IV. The longitudinal valleys lying between Greater and Lesser Himalayas are known as Duns.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: The Himalayas are young fold mountains, wider in Kashmir than in Arunachal, and the Greater Himalaya has asymmetrical folds with a granite core (NCERT). Duns are longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks, not between the Greater and Lesser Himalaya.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following Climatic regions of India according to Koeppen's scheme :
List-I (Type of Climate) - List-II (Areas)
A. Monsoon with short dry season - I. West coast of India, south of Goa
B. Monsoon with dry summer - II. Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu
C. Monsoon with dry winter - III. Most of North-East India
D. Semi-arid Steppe climate - IV. Northwestern Gujarat
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: In Koeppen's scheme for India (NCERT), Amw covers the west coast south of Goa, As the Coromandel coast, Cwg the Ganga plain and most of the North-East, and BShw parts of Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Within India, Ganga river basin has the largest catchment area. After that, following is the correct sequence in the decreasing order :
questions.x: Within India the Indus basin is about 3.2 lakh sq km, the Godavari about 3.1 lakh, the Krishna about 2.6 lakh and the Brahmaputra about 1.9 lakh sq km.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Peaty soils are one of the major soils of India. These are found in :
o: the areas of low rainfall with low leaching activity.
the areas of high temperature and high rainfall with intense leaching.
the areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation.
the areas of semi-arid climate with salinity.
questions.x: Peaty soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation, where dead organic matter piles up. Examples are Kerala and the Sundarbans.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In India, Sholas are :
o: Tropical forests found in the Bastar region
Tropical evergreen forests of Andaman & Nicobar islands
Moist deciduous forests in the North-eastern states
Temperate forests in the Anaimalai and Palani hills
questions.x: Sholas are temperate montane forests found in the high hills of the Western Ghats, such as the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Dharwar types of rocks are found in :
questions.x: Dharwar schist belts in Andhra Pradesh occur in the Nellore schist belt and parts of Chittoor and Anantapur districts. Kurnool has Cuddapah/Kurnool system rocks and the deltas have recent alluvium.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List-I (Wildlife Sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh) - List-II (Endangered Species)
A. Coringa - I. Great Indian Bustard
B. Gundla Brahmeswaram - II. Jerdon's Courser
C. Rollapadu - III. Saltwater Crocodile
D. Sri Lankamalleswara - IV. Tiger
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Coringa's mangroves hold saltwater crocodiles, Gundla Brahmeswaram is part of the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam tiger landscape, Rollapadu protects the Great Indian Bustard, and Sri Lankamalleswara is known for Jerdon's Courser.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List-I (Hunters / Nomadic tribes) - List-II (Region)
A. Pygmies - I. East Africa
B. Masai - II. Congo basin
C. Semangs - III. Borneo
D. Punan - IV. Malaysia
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Pygmies live in the Congo basin, the Masai are pastoral nomads of East Africa (Kenya and Tanzania), the Semangs live in the Malay peninsula and the Punan in Borneo.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement on the linguistic diversity of India :
o: In 1961 census, 1652 languages were listed as mother tongues in India.
Kachchi and Sindhi are Indo-European languages.
Austric languages are spoken by the tribal groups in Jharkhand.
questions.x: Dardic languages (such as Kashmiri and Shina) belong to the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-European family, not Sino-Tibetan. The 1961 census did list 1,652 mother tongues.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Match the following :
List-I (Slash and burn agriculture) - List-II (Practising region)
A. Ladang - I. Central America
B. Milpa - II. Indonesia
C. Roca - III. Central Africa
D. Masole - IV. Brazil
Choose the correct answer using the codes given below :
questions.x: Shifting cultivation is called Ladang in Indonesia and Malaysia, Milpa in Central America and Mexico, Roca in Brazil and Masole in Central Africa (Congo).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Following are the regions of Iron and Steel industry in the world :
I. The Atlantic coast region : The United States
II. The Ural region : Russia
III. The Ruhr region : Eastern Europe
IV. The North-eastern and Central parts : The United Kingdom
Which of the above are correctly matched ?
questions.x: The US Atlantic coast, Russia's Urals and the UK's north-eastern and central parts are iron and steel regions. The Ruhr is in Germany, in Western Europe, not Eastern Europe.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Trans-Siberian Railway runs between the stations in Russia from :
questions.x: Following the NCERT description, APPSC keyed the Trans-Siberian Railway as running from St. Petersburg in the west to Vladivostok on the Pacific coast. The final key accepts both option 1 (Moscow to Vladivostok) and option 3 (St. Petersburg to Vladivostok).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following states of India :
I. Punjab
II. Odisha
III. Haryana
IV. Tamil Nadu
Which of the above states have relatively high level of groundwater utilization ?
questions.x: Punjab, Haryana and Tamil Nadu draw on a very high share of their groundwater (NCERT). Odisha's groundwater use is low.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: Identify the incorrect statement on Wheat crop cultivation in India :
o: It is the second most important cereal crop.
It is a Rabi crop that requires a cool growing season.
It is chiefly grown in the Ganga-Satluj plains.
Black soil region of the Deccan is not suitable for wheat cultivation.
questions.x: Wheat is India's second most important cereal, a rabi crop grown mainly in the Ganga-Satluj plains. It is also grown in the black soil region of the Deccan (Maharashtra and MP), so option 4 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following oil fields of India :
I. Digboi
II. Moran
III. Kalol
IV. Naharkatiya
Which of the above oil fields are located in Assam ?
questions.x: Digboi, Moran and Naharkatiya are oil fields in Assam. Kalol is in Gujarat.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s: In India, most of the jute mills are located in :
questions.x: Most of India's jute mills line the Hugli river near Kolkata in West Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.s:
Consider the following erstwhile districts of Andhra Pradesh :
I. West Godavari
II. East Godavari
III. Visakhapatnam
IV. Srikakulam
In which of the above districts are coffee plantations mainly existing in their agency areas ?
questions.x: Andhra Pradesh's coffee grows mainly in the agency (tribal hill) areas of the old Visakhapatnam (Araku, Paderu) and East Godavari districts.
